statement_refuted: A cap-one joint density for a dependent pair, together with an independent cap-one scalar, suffices to transfer the non-null physical-chain curved-fiber density bound with a universal constant.
counterexample_summary: For fixed A=3[[1,1,0],[1,0,1],[0,1,0]], all three eigenvalues have modulus >1. Let X be uniform [0,1], independent of (Y,Z) with unit joint density on E_N={e^-N/N<=y<=1/N, 0<=z<=1/(Ny)}. Then p_(Z|Y=y)<=1 but P(0<=X^TAX<=9/N)>=1/(4sqrt(N)), forcing any bound for the weakened interface to be at least sqrt(N)/36. Y,Z are dependent, so this does not refute QFORM.
